techniques_scope.description:
Precision filter for the resolved `techniques`. Trades recall against CVE-specificity:
- `all` (default): every linked technique, including those derived from broad/Pillar CWEs (e.g. CWE-20 'Improper Input Validation'). Maximum recall, but unrelated CVEs sharing a generic CWE converge on the same coarse set — check `techniques_provenance` to tell which.
- `specific`: drop techniques attributable only to a generic CWE's CAPEC closure, keeping those tied to the CVE's specific weaknesses. Higher precision; may be empty when the CVE has no specific ATT&CK mapping (the honest answer for such CVEs).
Ignored when `techniques` is not in `include`.

info.description:
Turn a CVE, IOC, product, package, weakness, or ATT&CK entity into a response you can
use in a ticket, report, or agent workflow. The API returns severity, exploit evidence, weakness analysis,
ATT&CK mappings, defensive guidance, and prioritization data.

This reference covers 33 operations: 29 synchronous enrichment, search, and assessment endpoints, plus
4 async submit and status operations.

## Make your first request

```bash
curl -X POST https://crimsoncrawler.com/v1/enrich/cve \
  -H "apikey: YOUR_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"cve_id": "CVE-2024-3400"}'
```

The default CVE response includes details, EPSS, KEV, weaknesses, attack patterns, ATT&CK techniques,
technique predictions, and NIST controls.

## Choose an endpoint

| Category | Operations | Use it for |
|---|---:|---|
| Enrichment | 17 | Resolve 1 entity, or enrich up to 50 mixed items with `/v1/enrich/batch`. |
| Search | 8 | Find CVEs, threat records, known-exploited vulnerabilities, vendors, and public exploit material. |
| Assessment | 4 | Compare technique coverage, vulnerability exposure, group exposure, or an IOC portfolio. |
| Async enrichment | 4 | Submit text, files, or an asset inventory, then poll for the finished report. |

## Control response depth

Most enrichment endpoints, every assessment endpoint, and `/v1/search/cve` accept `include`. Passing it
selects the exact response layers and replaces that endpoint's default set.

```json
{
  "cve_id": "CVE-2024-3400",
  "include": ["details", "epss", "kev", "techniques", "ssvc", "summary"]
}
```

Requesting fewer layers is usually faster. Each billable v1 call still consumes 1 request unit, regardless of depth.

## Read the response

Fields excluded by `include` return as `null` or empty arrays. If requested intelligence is unavailable,
a `200` response keeps the data that resolved and records the gap in `errors[]`.

Common HTTP outcomes:

| Status | Meaning |
|---:|---|
| `200` | Synchronous request completed. Check `errors[]` for partial source failures. |
| `202` | Async enrichment accepted; poll the returned identifier. |
| `401` | API key is missing, invalid, or inactive. |
| `404` | Async identifier is missing, expired, or owned by another key. |
| `422` | Request shape, field value, or cross-field combination is invalid. |
| `429` | Gateway quota is exhausted, or an async key already has 20 jobs in flight. |
| `500` | An unexpected server error crossed the API's last-resort error boundary. |
| `503` | Async queue state could not be verified, so no job was accepted. |

Each operation below lists only the statuses it can return and its exact success schema.

## Run longer jobs

`POST /v1/artifact-enrich` and `POST /v1/inventory-enrich` return `202` with an `enrichment_id`. Poll the
matching `GET /v1/*-enrich/{enrichment_id}` route until `status` is `done` or `error`. Status polls consume
no plan units.

Each key can run 3 async jobs at once and hold 20 running or queued jobs. A full queue returns `429` with
`enrichment_queue_full`.

## Authenticate

Send your API key in the `apikey` header. `x-api-key` is also accepted. Keep keys out of source control,
URLs, request bodies, and browser-side code.

See [Quick Start](/docs/quickstart/) for a working integration, [Authentication](/docs/authentication/) for
limits and key rotation, and [Enrichment Depth](/docs/guides/enrichment-chains/) for endpoint-specific
`include` values.

post.description:
Submit security text or files for asynchronous Artifact Enrichment.

Returns an `enrichment_id` with HTTP 202. Poll
`/v1/artifact-enrich/{enrichment_id}` for stage progress and the finished report.

Supply up to 1,000,000 characters in `text`, up to 20 base64-encoded files, or both. Supported
inputs include scan exports, vulnerability reports, advisories, email, spreadsheets, and plain
text. The report resolves detected CVEs, products, packages, weaknesses, techniques, and
indicators into evidence, SSVC decisions, PATCH/BLOCK/WATCH/INFO actions, prioritized work,
attack paths, defensive guidance, citations, and requested machine-readable exports.

`include` selects report sections; it does not reduce the evidence used for core decisions.
Decisions, scores, grades, references, and prioritized actions are always returned. The allowed
section names and export formats are defined in the request schema.

Submission consumes one request unit. Polling consumes none. Each API key can run 3 Artifact or
Inventory Enrichments at once and can hold 20 running or queued jobs across both engines. Jobs
beyond the running limit remain `queued`; a full queue returns 429. If queue state cannot be
verified, the request returns 503 and no job is created.

get.description:
Poll an Artifact Enrichment until it finishes.

Returns overall `progress`, ordered stage and substage progress, a rolling event feed, and one
of these states:

- `queued`: waiting for a slot; `queue_position` is the number of jobs ahead
- `running`: enrichment is in progress
- `done`: `result` contains the completed `ArtifactEnrichmentReport`
- `error`: `error` contains the terminal failure

that submitted the job can read it, and a different key receives 404. Anonymous, keyless, and
direct MCP submissions use a capability URL, so possession of the job UUID is sufficient to
read the result. A missing, expired, malformed, or owner-hidden identifier returns 404 or 422.

Find vulnerabilities affecting a product and enrich each matched CVE.

Searches by product name, version, and vendor using CPE matching, then runs every matched CVE
through the same multi-source chain as `/v1/enrich/cve`. Supply `vendor` to narrow CPE matches
and `version` to hard-filter discovered CVEs to those affecting that release.

The include options drive the per-CVE enrichment depth (each value behaves exactly as it does on
`/v1/enrich/cve`); the product-level extras roll those results up across the matched set.

**Include options**

Per-CVE enrichment (applied to each matched CVE):

- `details` — core CVE data (CVSS, severity, description, references)
- `epss` — EPSS exploit probability score and percentile
- `kev` — Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog status
- `cwe` — root cause weakness classification
- `capec` — attack patterns for the weakness
- `techniques` — linked ATT&CK techniques
- `tie` — technique likelihood predictions
- `navigator` — ATT&CK Navigator layer JSON
- `misp` — matching threat intelligence events
- `knowledgebase` — related knowledge-base context
- `web` — live web search for exploits and advisories
- `web_scrape` — scraped article text on the top web results (requires `web`)
- `affected_products` — confirmed vulnerable software with CPE strings
- `poc` — proof-of-concept exploits from GitHub
- `groups` — threat actor groups using the linked techniques
- `software` — malware and tools using the linked techniques
- `campaigns` — threat campaigns using the linked techniques
- `mitigations` — defensive courses of action per technique
- `detections` — detection data sources per technique
- `defend` — D3FEND defensive techniques

- `summary` — AI-generated product-level brief over the matched CVE set
